notes: Running words 704, within 585–715. Dialogue is about a third of the words.
Elen hands Mali the lamp and does not call Pero; she looks at the forest. This is a silent hint that she knows about the tower (consistent with sec-dafi note that Cynyr and Elen suspect).
The sneeze is rendered as 'A… a… Atishŵ!' with a define gloss (sŵn + mwg) because tisian is Pennod 5. Segment speaker is char-dafi for audio only; the reader does not yet know who it is.
Lint: 'Mae mwg' with an indefinite subject is affirmative mae, which is correct; the negative of indefinite subjects (Does dim) is Pennod 6, and this chapter avoids indefinite negatives entirely.
No 'A ti?' item: second-person forms arrive in Pennod 5.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md): glosses no longer use a word before the reader meets it. s001's 'oer ↔ cynnes' (cynnes first at s003) moves to s003 as 'cynnes ↔ oer', beside the fire vignette; s036's 'pell ↔ agos' (agos first at s037) is now 'pell: Cwm Helyg … Llundain' (the Pennod 1 map), and s037 gets 'agos ↔ pell'; the yma/yno gloss at s049 came after both first uses, so s013 now has 'yma = yn y stabl' and s024 'yno ↔ yma'. Meta-language: Gramadeg header 'Ateb' (a Pennod 12 word) is now '✓ / ✗'; 'dim newid' is now 'll → ll'. Pensa: A a10 'yn ___ (llwyd) → llwyd' gave the answer in the cue; it is now a two-gap item that sets unchanged llwyd beside dawel (Enghraifft likewise: hen … dywyll); b1 also fitted agor, now cued by the cold; A a6/a8/a9/a11 and C c1/c3/c6 accept full answers, pronouns, the fronted identification and 'ar y llwybr' (where Pero runs at s086).

grammar.nodyn_en: With a definite subject (a name, y/yr/'r + noun), Mae becomes Ydy in questions: Ydy Pero yma? Answer Ydy or Nac ydy. The southern negative is Dyw … ddim: Dyw Pero ddim yma. A yes/no identification question (Pero yw e? Tân yw e?) is answered Ie or Nage instead.
